title: Tenant-aware limiter cutover sanitizer and graceful outage mode
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Recent incidents exposed an operational gap when the centralized admission limiter partials out or the lease fabric delays. Customers can see sudden 'token refused' errors and opaque 429s that are hard to correlate to region failovers. We need a robust, tenant-aware cutover path for limiter partitions that preserves SLOs for high-tier customers, prevents long tail unfairness, and allows safe rollbacks.

Goal: Implement a runtime 'cutover sanitizer' and graceful outage mode for the limiter layer that: 1) immediately detects degraded/partitioned limiter nodes; 2) places affected tenants into a local best-effort mode with bounded risk (local token buckets + forgiveness window); 3) mirrors deltas to a durable "shadow quota" store for reconciliation; 4) uses a probe-driven circuit-breaker to restore normal enforcement with no silent over-issuance; 5) surfaces deterministic telemetry and an operator playbook to mitigate SEV escalation.

Technical approach (high level):
- Detection: add heartbeats + difference checks (apply-lag-ms and delta anomalies) to quickly classify a limiter instance as degraded. Use EWMA of success ratio over 10s window and a fast path for large surge detection.
- Outage mode (local best-effort): affected frontends switch to a conservative local token-bucket per-tenant (local_bucket_size = min(ceil(0.5 * committed_rate_window), 100 tokens)) with an exponential decay of granted burst capacity. Introduce a 'token forgiveness' budget that allows a bounded overspend during short outages; forgiven tokens are recorded to the shadow ledger.
- Shadow quota mirror: local deltas (grants, forgives) are appended to a durable, append-only queue (S3-backed segments or existing quota-store topic) and reconciled by a background reconciler when the central limiter returns. Reconciler uses idempotent apply and tenant priorities to resolve conflicts.
- Probe-driven recovery: implement a circuit-breaker that switches from outage->probe->recovered states. Probe policy: 5 probe requests per-second for each affected tenant across a 30s window; success threshold 80% over 15s to transition to recovered. Probes are rate-limited and distributed to avoid thundering recovery.
- Fairness heuristics: to avoid starvation during partials, use EWMA-based deficit tracking combined with tenant weight normalization. During outage mode, allocate local capacity proportionally to weight * (1 + recent_usage_factor) with safeguards so a runaway client can't exhaust local forgiveness.
- SLO and rollout: enforce per-tenant SLO mappings. For enterprise (paid) tenants, default to more conservative decay but higher forgiveness budget. Canary rollout with automated rollback based on error budget burn and 5xx/429 spikes.

Observability / metrics to add:
- limiter.outage_mode_count (per region)
- limiter.mirror_lag_ms
- limiter.tokens_forgiven_total (by tenant tier)
- limiter.local_burst_absorption
- limiter.fairness_violation_rate
- limiter.recovery_probe_success_rate
- dashboard: per-route SLO burn vs tokens_forgiven overlay

Operational playbook (brief):
1) Automated detection triggers outage mode and annotates incidents with affected tenants.
2) On-call inspects dashboard (mirror_lag_ms, forgiveness rate) and can either accelerate or pause reconcilers.
3) If reconcilers are healthy and probe success rate > 80%, system will auto-recover; otherwise operator can initiate controlled drain and redirect traffic to dedicated capacity.

Why this is different: Instead of pure fail-open or hard 429s, this design accepts bounded risk with a durable accounting strategy and deterministic reconciliation so that customer-perceived failures are reduced while maintaining global correctness once the limiter returns. It explicitly ties behavior to tenant tiers and SLOs to reduce business impact.
acceptance_criteria: Local outage mode can be enabled via config and defaults to off
Outage mode preserves P0/P1 tenant SLOs with fewer user-visible 429 spikes during simulated limiter partitions
Shadow mirror reliably persists local deltas with end-to-end idempotent reconciliation in recovery tests
Probe-driven circuit-breaker transitions are logged and metrics exposed; canary rollout triggers rollback on threshold breach
Load tests show fairness_violation_rate < 0.2% for 99th percentile client across synthetic burst workloads
